assets.caption: Georgian Colonial American, roof penetration discipline: an authored position, not a retrieved one.
assets.alt_text: A measured diagram of the roof penetration discipline strategy proposed for Georgian Colonial American. No historical precedent exists for this slot, so there is nothing to photograph and the drawing has to carry the argument. Nothing penetrates the entrance slope of the roof except a chimney or a dormer set in the bay rhythm; every modern penetration — plumbing vent, flue, fan, array — goes on the rear slope, below the ridge line and out of the approach cone. Dimensions must be shown, because the whole claim is that the proposal follows rules the style already contains.

assets.caption: Georgian Colonial American, construction type: masonry-veneer-over-frame — wrong, and why.
assets.alt_text: A Georgian Colonial American house showing construction type executed as masonry-veneer-over-frame. This is the error condition. THE SLOT THAT DID NOT EXIST. A single 3 5/8 in wythe cannot be laid in Flemish or English bond, because both are through-bonds defined by headers passing into the wall's depth: a 'Flemish bond' veneer is half-bricks glued to a backup and the giveaway is that the header and the stretcher have the same face. It also collapses the reveal from 4-8 in to nothing and leaves the water table and belt course with no wall-thickness change to weather. Three separate slots in this kit are unbuildable on a veneer and until 0.2.0 nothing recorded why. The frame must be close enough that the construction type reads at full detail and wide enough to show what it sits against, so the viewer can see the mistake in context rather than as an abstraction.

assets.caption: Georgian Colonial American, porch rail: the period dimension against the code minimum.
assets.alt_text: A dimensioned comparison drawing. Period: Rail height 30-33 in, balusters at 4-6 in centres. Code: 36 in minimum guard height; 4 in maximum sphere between balusters (IRC R312.1.2, R312.1.3). Resolution: The baluster spacing conflict is resolved by taking the 4 in end of the period band, which is period-correct anyway. The height conflict is resolved by raising the whole assembly — a taller plinth under the balusters and a taller newel — rather than by lengthening the baluster, which changes its turned proportion. assets.caption: Georgian Colonial American, stair type: the period dimension against the code minimum.
assets.alt_text: A dimensioned comparison drawing. Period: Riser 7.5-8.5 in, tread 9-10.5 in. Code: Riser 7.75 in maximum, tread 10 in minimum (IRC R311.7.5). Resolution: A period-correct principal stair is not buildable as drawn. Taking the shallow end of the period band (7.75 in riser, 10 in tread) is legal and is inside the historical range, but it adds a riser per storey and lengthens the run by about 10 in, which eats the passage the plan is organised around. Where the passage cannot absorb it, add a winder-free landing and turn the stair earlier rather than reducing the passage width below the 10 ft minimum.. Both conditions drawn at the same scale and overlaid, so the size of the compromise is visible rather than argued.

assets.caption: Georgian Colonial American, newel & balustrade: the period dimension against the code minimum.
assets.alt_text: A dimensioned comparison drawing. Period: Handrail 30-32 in above the tread nosing. Code: 34 in minimum, 38 in maximum (IRC R311.7.8.1). Resolution: Set the rail at 34 in — the code minimum and only 2 in above the period band, which is within the tolerance of the ramp-and-ease anyway. Do not stretch the balusters: lengthen the newel and re-cut the ramp, which is where the 2 in should be absorbed.. Both conditions drawn at the same scale and overlaid, so the size of the compromise is visible rather than argued.

assets.caption: Neo-Eclectic, primary cladding: shingle-continuous-field — wrong, and why.
assets.alt_text: A Neo-Eclectic house showing primary cladding executed as shingle-continuous-field. This is the error condition. Members bottom to top: Bed mould, cyma reversa (gola rovescia) (4p), Fillet over the bed mould (listello) (1p), Corona (gocciolatoio) (5p), Fillet over the corona (listello) (1p), Torus under the cymatium (toro) (1p), Cymatium, ovolo (ovolo) (4p). Every dimension is generated by the proportion engine from the pack, so the drawing and the data cannot silently disagree.

provenance.source: Vignola, Regola delli cinque ordini d'architettura, Rome 1562, Tavole IV-VIII
